`free`: display the amount of memory in use and free.

## Synopsis

<strong>free</strong> \[<strong>-b</strong>\|<strong>-k</strong>\|<strong>-m</strong>\|<strong>-h</strong>\]

## Description

<strong>free</strong> prints the computer's memory: the total (the RAM installed), what is in use, and what is free.

Before measuring it runs a full garbage collection 20 times, since Lua's collector frees some objects (those with finalizers, for one) only on a later cycle; so <em>used</em> is what is really held, not garbage waiting to be collected.

## Options

<strong>-b</strong>
: Show amounts in bytes.

<strong>-k</strong>
: Show amounts in KiB (the default).

<strong>-m</strong>
: Show amounts in MiB.

<strong>-h</strong>
: Show amounts in human-readable form, with a unit after each: <strong>B</strong>, <strong>Ki</strong>, <strong>Mi</strong> or <strong>Gi</strong>.

Each option is a separate argument; the last unit given wins, and <strong>-h</strong> wins over any unit.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 for an unknown option or if the memory could not be read.

## Notes

There is no swap, so there is no <strong>Swap:</strong> line, and no buffer or cache columns. The total is the RAM installed above what the firmware itself holds.

## See also

<strong>df</strong>(1), <strong>ps</strong>(1)
